questions.text: What is the minimum number of resources required to ensure that deadlock will never occur, if there are currently three processes [latex]P_{1}[/latex],[latex]P_{2}[/latex] and [latex]P_{3}[/latex] running in a system whose maximum demand for the resources of same type are 3, 4, and 5 respectively.
questions.solution:
Worst case: each process holds one less than its maximum: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 resources, and all wait.

One more resource lets one process finish: 9 + 1 = 10.

Answer: 10

questions.text: A computer has 16 pages of virtual address space but the size of main memory is only four frames. Initially the memory is empty. A program references the virtual pages in the order 0, 2, 4, 5, 2, 4, 3, 11, 2, 10. How many page faults occur if LRU page replacement algorithm is used?
questions.solution:
LRU with 4 frames:

- 0, 2, 4, 5: 4 faults
- 2, 4: hits
- 3: fault, evict 0 (5)
- 11: fault, evict 5 (6)
- 2: hit
- 10: fault, evict 4 (7)

Answer: 7

questions.text:
Using the page table shown below, translate the physical address 25 to virtual address. The address length is 16 bits and page size is 2048 words while the size of the physical memory is four frames.
[latex]\begin{array}{lcc} \text { Page } & \text { Present }(1-In , 0-Out) & \text { Frame } \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & - \end{array}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Page size = 2048. Physical address 25 is in frame 0 with offset 25.

Frame 0 holds page 2 (from the table). Virtual address = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2048 + 25 = 4121.

Answer: 4121

questions.text:
Consider the following segment table in segmentation scheme :
[latex]\begin{array}{|l|l|l|} \hline \text { Segment ID } & \text { Base } & \text { Limit } \\ \hline 0 & 200 & 200 \\ \hline 1 & 5000 & 1210 \\ \hline 2 & 1527 & 498 \\ \hline 3 & 2500 & 50 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
What happens if the logical address requested is - Segment Id 2 and offset 1000?
questions.solution:
Segment 2 has limit 498. Offset 1000 [latex]\gt[/latex] 498, so the address is outside the segment and the hardware raises a trap (addressing error).

Answer: A trap is generated

questions.text: There are 200 tracks on a disc platter and the pending requests have come in the order - 36, 69, 167, 76, 42, 51, 126, 12 and 199. Assume the arm is located at the 100th track and moving towards track 200. If sequence of disc access is 126, 167, 199, 12, 36, 42, 51, 69 and 76 then which disc access scheduling policy is used?
questions.solution:
The head moves up: 126, 167, 199 (to the end). Then it jumps back to the start and again moves up: 12, 36, 42, 51, 69, 76.

Servicing in only one direction with a return jump is C-SCAN. (SCAN/elevator would come down: 76, 69, ... 12.)

Answer: C-SCAN
